analyst_view.overall: Brighton are 2nd but lost 2-0 at Hull last time out, conceding twice in added time after Costinha was sent off; he is suspended here. Fabian Hurzeler's side also play Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League on Thursday, only three days before this game, though he is resting players such as Diego Gomez for it. Mitoma, Ferguson, Tzimas and Yohanna are out, and Malick Yalcouye was injured over the international break (6-10 weeks), which the numbers do not list. Newcastle, 13th under Matthias Jaissle, came back to draw 2-2 at Arsenal and have a free week; Joelinton and goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen are out, and Lewis Hall limped off at Arsenal, though Jaissle hoped it was only cramp. The numbers already count Hall as out and Simon Hooper's high card rate.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals: 1.9 for Brighton and 1.1 for Newcastle, with both sides' poor recent finishing already counted. They also treat Lewis Hall as out, which lowers Newcastle's goals and raises Brighton's; Jaissle hoped it was just cramp, but that is not confirmed. Brighton lose Costinha and Yalcouye, and Newcastle are without Joelinton. Nothing points clearly either way, so I stay at about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.8 corners, 5.2 for Brighton and 4.6 for Newcastle, already lowered a little because both have won fewer corners lately. Brighton's possession game and Newcastle's direct wide play both produce corners, and the team news does not change that, so I stay at about 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.4 cards. That already includes Simon Hooper's high card rate (4.5 a game) and both teams being booked more than usual lately, so the figure is already high. There is no derby edge or new ban beyond Costinha, who is already out, so I stay at about 5.4.

shots.text: The numbers expect 26.4 shots, 16.0 from Brighton, which already includes their high shot count over the last six games. Brighton play a European game on Thursday, only three days before, while Newcastle have a free week, and the numbers do not count that. Hurzeler is resting some players, so the effect should be small: I take about 3% off, to about 25.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 8.6 shots on target, already lowered because both teams have hit the target less than expected lately. Brighton's quick turnaround could cost a little sharpness, but they wasted good chances at Hull rather than failing to create them, so I stay at about 8.6.
